shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Default tier for a card sitting in a list.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Open/expanded card, focused field companion, summary card, slider thumb.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: PIN sheet, alerts, floating action bar — sits above chrome itself.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: System-wide duration; collapses to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Filled Button
components.description: Primary full-width or auto-width action; tint fill, presses to tint-press.
components.css: .ds-btn-filled { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; background: #0062cc; color: #ffffff; border: none; transition: background 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-btn-filled:hover { background: #0058b8; } .ds-btn-filled:active { background: #004fa6; } .ds-btn-filled:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0062cc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Criterion Card (resting/raised)
components.description: Solid card holding a criterion's name, weight pill, and score; lifts from resting to raised when expanded.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.05); border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.04), 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.08); overflow: hidden; transition: box-shadow 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), background 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-card.ds-open { box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.06), 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.12); } .ds-card-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; min-height: 44px; padding: 11px 16px; } .ds-card-label { flex: 1; font-size: 1.0625rem; } .ds-card-pill { padding: 3px 9px; border-radius: 980px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; background: rgba(120,120,128,0.12); color: #55555c; } .ds-card-score { font-family: ui-rounded, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 1.75rem; font-weight: 600; color: #6a6a72; min-width: 2.6ch; text-align: right; }

components.name: Glass Nav Bar
components.description: Sticky translucent chrome; blurs content as it scrolls beneath.
components.html: Team Alpha
components.css: .ds-nav { position: sticky; top: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; background: color-mix(in srgb, #f2f2f7 82%, transparent); backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(24px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(24px); border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; } .ds-nav-back { color: #0062cc; font-size: 1.0625rem; background: none; border: none; } .ds-nav-title { font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-nav-spacer { min-width: 44px; }

components.name: PIN Keypad Sheet
components.description: Glass bottom sheet with dot indicators and a circular numeric keypad; replaces the system keyboard for judge sign-in.
components.css: .ds-sheet { width: 100%; max-width: 420px; padding: 6px 24px 22px; background: color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 90%, transparent); backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(24px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(24px); border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06); border-radius: 16px 16px 0 0; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08), 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.18); } .ds-pin-dots { display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 16px; margin: 0 0 20px; } .ds-pin-dot { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(120,120,128,0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.05); } .ds-pin-dot.ds-filled { background: #0062cc; border-color: transparent; } .ds-keypad { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 14px; } .ds-key { aspect-ratio: 1; min-height: 60px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(120,120,128,0.12); color: #10101a; font-size: 1.625rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-key:active { background: rgba(120,120,128,0.2); transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0062cc; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: The scoresheet replaced its prior "everything is a row" grouped-list grammar with Apple's own card-and-glass material system — the language of Wallet, App Store, Health, and Control Center. This was a direct, user-pinned reversal of the standing preference (see PRODUCT.md, Brand Commitments), not a roll outcome, and it shipped as a genuine two-material hierarchy: floating, continuous-corner cards hold every piece of data, and a translucent vibrancy layer is reserved for chrome alone. The system declines the web category's glassmorphism pastiche — rainbow blur cards adrift on a gradient background — in favor of Apple's own restraint: one tint, three shadow tiers, and glass confined strictly to the elements that float above content rather than carrying it. A card that holds a score or a field is always solid and opaque, so text on it keeps full AA contrast regardless of what is moving in the blur above it.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials, never mixed: solid opaque cards for data, translucent glass for chrome only.
Three-tier corner scale (20 / 16 / 10px) and three-tier shadow scale (resting / raised / floating), both keyed to a surface's role, not its size.
One tint carries every interactive element; shadows and glass never substitute for it as an affordance cue.
A custom on-screen numeric PIN keypad replaces the judge's old text-field PIN entry; no system keyboard appears during sign-in.
Both themes follow the device, with a manual override, because the judge works in a dimmed auditorium and the organizer on a lit laptop.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: `--tint` carries every interactive element and nothing decorative. Shadows and glass are depth cues, never affordance cues.

rules.name: The Two Materials, Never Mixed Rule
rules.body: Chrome (nav bar, floating action bar, alerts, PIN sheet) is translucent glass; content (every card holding data) is solid and opaque. A card is never blurred; a chrome surface never carries body data directly.

rules.name: The Card Comes Forward Rule
rules.body: The signature interaction — tapping a criterion card to unfold its control in place — lifts the card's shadow tier from resting to raised as it opens, so the expansion reads as the card advancing toward the viewer, not merely growing taller.

rules.name: The Glass Never Carries Data Rule
rules.body: Nothing with a shadow tier above resting is glass except the three named chrome exceptions (nav, floating action bar, alerts, PIN sheet). Every other floating/raised surface is solid.

dos: Do keep every card that holds data (criterion, participant, standing, setup field) solid and opaque at --bg-card-*, never blurred.
Do confine backdrop-filter to the four named chrome surfaces: nav bar, floating action bar, alerts, PIN sheet.
Do scale corner radius by role — 20px page-level, 16px chrome sheet, 10px control — not by visual size alone.
Do lift a card's shadow tier (resting → raised) when it opens or gains focus, as the honest depth cue for state change.
Do keep --font-num with tabular-nums on every score, weight, and total so a changing number never reflows its row.

Do follow prefers-color-scheme with the manual data-theme override, and keep both dark-mode CSS blocks in sync since they are deliberately duplicated to let the override beat the media query without specificity tricks.
donts: Don't apply glass to a surface that carries body text or a score — the auditorium-dim judge's AA contrast depends on staying off the blur.
Don't use a single heavy drop shadow. Every elevated surface uses the two-layer ambient+key pairing at one of the three named tiers.
Don't invent a fourth shadow tier or a nested-card radius outside 20/16/10px; the contract's earlier 14px guess never shipped and should not be revived.

Don't introduce a kicker/eyebrow label, a hard-offset neobrutalist shadow, a glyph icon font, or a system display face — none of these exist in the shipped system, and none should be canonized as a rule for future surfaces even if a future build ships one under time pressure.
